case: Ball flight: data consistency (SkillCorner 3-D ball, 10 Hz)
physics: drag ODE with free gravity, fitted per flight
measured: g = 6.09 m/s² [6.02, 6.18] over 2601 flights (simulated flights, same fit: 9.88)
verdict: physics HELPED as a check: the broadcast ball height is not physically consistent (apparent gravity far below 9.81 at every launch speed, so not backspin lift); drag and spin cannot be identified from it

case: Ball flight: landing point from the first half of the flight
physics: drag_free_g (best of vacuum / drag with g = 9.81 / drag with free g); hybrid trees
baseline: ml (best of quadratic extrapolation / boosted trees)
measured: median landing error: physics 3.27 m, hybrid 2.55 m, data-only 2.44 m (1282 test flights)
verdict: physics did NOT help against trained trees: they learn this data's own (non-physical) height dynamics, which a g = 9.81 model cannot follow; physics does beat untrained extrapolation (7.51 m)

case: Ball flight from 2-D tracking (Metrica-type, no height)
physics: Cramer-Rao bound of the drag-Magnus fit
measured: std of vertical launch speed 0.34 m/s (3-D) vs 222 m/s (2-D)
verdict: ill-posed in 2-D: elevation, spin and drag trade off; do not fit them without height

physics: Spearman pitch control, 5 physical parameters fitted
baseline: logistic regression / boosted trees on geometric features
measured: fit on match 1, test on 2: fitted pitch control 0.1503 vs logistic 0.1737, diff -0.0234 [-0.0477, +0.0001]; fit on match 2, test on 1: fitted pitch control 0.1927 vs logistic 0.1891, diff +0.0036 [-0.0271, +0.0367]; with 100 training passes: fitted pitch control 0.1619, logistic 0.2183, trees 0.2526; unfitted pitch control (0 passes) 0.1925
verdict: physics HELPED with little data (lower log-loss than every data-only model up to a few hundred passes, unfitted or fitted) and is better calibrated; at full data it matches the best data-only model (gain not significant in both directions)

case: Speed and metabolic power from noisy tracking (simulated, known truth)
physics: constant-acceleration Kalman-RTS, noise by maximum likelihood
baseline: best Savitzky-Golay window (chosen with the truth: an optimistic baseline)
measured: metabolic-power RMSE 25 Hz/20 cm: 18.7 vs 23.8 W/kg; 25 Hz/5 cm: 15.3 vs 16.3 W/kg; 10 Hz/20 cm: 20.7 vs 28.8 W/kg; 10 Hz/5 cm: 16.7 vs 17.8 W/kg
verdict: physics HELPED (lower error in every case, calibrated intervals); the gain is largest against an untuned window. Caveat: the simulated motion follows a model close to the filter's

case: Metabolic power on Metrica (real, no ground truth)
baseline: the same on raw differences / Savitzky-Golay
measured: noise fitted 0.5 cm; team mean metabolic power, all samples: raw_differences 68.0, savitzky_golay_0.5s 13.7, kalman_rts 45.1 W/kg; physically plausible samples only: raw_differences 7.4, savitzky_golay_0.5s 7.1, kalman_rts 7.3 W/kg
verdict: physics HELPED as a gate, not as a smoother: a few tracking jumps (impossible speed or acceleration) dominate the match mean whatever the filter; removing them with human limits makes the methods agree. The provider data are already smooth (noise ~mm), so the smoother itself changes little

case: Player position 1s ahead (Metrica, train match 1, test match 2)
physics: constant velocity / decaying acceleration; trees on the constant-velocity residual (+ reachable-set projection)
baseline: boosted trees on the past second
measured: mean error: CV 0.56 m, physics 0.49 m; all data: trees 0.38 m, residual 0.38 m; 100 samples: trees 0.99 m, residual 0.52 m; unreachable trees predictions 0.05 %
verdict: physics prior HELPED with little data (47 % lower error); matched with all data (-0.5 %)

case: Player position 2s ahead (Metrica, train match 1, test match 2)
physics: constant velocity / decaying acceleration; trees on the constant-velocity residual (+ reachable-set projection)
baseline: boosted trees on the past second
measured: mean error: CV 1.98 m, physics 1.79 m; all data: trees 1.42 m, residual 1.43 m; 100 samples: trees 2.55 m, residual 1.92 m; unreachable trees predictions 0.03 %
verdict: physics prior HELPED with little data (25 % lower error); matched with all data (-0.2 %)

physics: intercept-time features: open goal fraction, keeper margin, blockers
baseline: standard logistic xG (distance, angle, body part, context)
verdict: physics did NOT help: no measurable gain over shot geometry with ~2600 training shots; case dropped
